results.summary_before: This design implements a simplified version of the Chrome Dino game on a VGA display, where a dinosaur jumps over obstacles and cannot lose. It is used by connecting a button to input pin 0 and a VGA display to the outputs, then pressing the button to make the dinosaur jump. External hardware required includes a VGA display and a button with a power source. The documentation is brief and does not mention any testing or silicon results.

results.summary_before: This circuit takes eight digital inputs, passes some through NOT, XOR and AND gates, and drives eight outputs connected to a 7-segment display. Inputs IN0, IN1 and IN2 are tied together as a single signal A that feeds three NOT gates driving OUT0 to OUT2, while IN3 to IN5 pass through directly and IN5 with IN6 feed an XOR and IN6 with IN7 feed an AND. The documentation gives a full output logic table for testing, though the external hardware section is left as an unfilled template. Despite the title RandomNum, the described behaviour is combinational logic rather than a random number generator.

results.summary_before: This Wokwi design displays the letter P on a 7-segment display when a secret code is entered on its eight switches. The author started from the template and customised the segment outputs, and the documentation deliberately withholds the code so that users can try to discover it. No external hardware is required beyond the display. The project is a first Wokwi design and is presented as a learning exercise, with the pin names still carrying the template's default labels.
